independent_solution.main_law_or_principle: Newton's First Law at terminal velocity (Drag = Weight - Upthrust)
independent_solution.calculation_or_logic:
Let $V$ be the volume of the object and $\rho_x$ be its density. Weight $W = V\rho_x g$. Upthrust $U = V\rho_f g$. Drag $F_d = kv$. At terminal velocity, $kv = Vg(\rho_x - \rho_f)$.
Case 1: $k(5v_0) = Vg(\rho_x - \rho)$.
Case 2: $k(v_0) = Vg(\rho_x - 3\rho)$.
Dividing Case 1 by Case 2: $5 = (\rho_x - \rho) / (\rho_x - 3\rho)$.
$5(\rho_x - 3\rho) = \rho_x - \rho \implies 5\rho_x - 15\rho = \rho_x - \rho \implies 4\rho_x = 14\rho \implies \rho_x = 3.5\rho = \frac{7}{2}\rho$.

notes: The physics is sound and the algebraic manipulation is appropriate for the target level.
